title: Senior asks: index.php sends home.html with PHP when there is no ?action. What is the better way?
options: Let the web server send home.html as a static file. PHP then runs only for the API
Keep it. PHP is faster than the web server for files
Put the HTML inside a PHP string
explain: A web server sends static files fast, with caching headers, and without starting PHP. Your PHP code should handle only the API. For php -S and Apache the rewrite rule can skip existing files.

title: Senior asks: you move the project to full Symfony. #[Route('/files/{name}', methods: ['DELETE'])] on a method. What does it replace in your code?
options: The ACTION_METHODS const and the checkAction() 405 check
explain: Symfony routing maps path and HTTP method to a controller method and answers 405 itself when the method is wrong. So the ACTION_METHODS map and checkAction() are not needed. The `match ($action)` is also gone: one method per route.

title: Senior asks: an Excel CSV is saved as Windows-1252, so é is the single byte E9. read() returns it and the API calls json_encode(). What is the result?
explain: json_encode() only accepts UTF-8. The byte E9 is not valid UTF-8, so it returns false (or throws with JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR). The API would send a broken answer. Fix: check or convert the encoding when you read the CSV (mb_convert_encoding) and answer 422 for bad files.

pr.title: Add CORS so other sites can use the API
pr.author: copilot
pr.body: The front end of a partner is on another domain. Allow all origins.

explain: The API has no login and DELETE removes files. With * every website in the world can call it from a visitor's browser. Allow only the known partner origin, or no CORS at all, and add authentication before you open the API.

title: array_map() with one array and string keys. What does this print?
explain: With ONE array, array_map() keeps the keys, string keys too. With two or more arrays it gives a list with keys 0, 1, 2. If you need keys changed, use array_combine() or a foreach.

title: A grid of 3 rows. What does this print?
explain: fill([]) puts the SAME array object in all 3 slots. A push through one row shows in all rows. Make separate arrays: Array.from({ length: 3 }, () => []).

title: A merge commit M on main broke the site. It is already pushed. How do you undo it safely?
options: git reset --hard HEAD~1 and force push
explain: A merge commit has two parents, so git revert needs -m to know which side to keep. -m 1 means: keep the first parent (main). The revert is a new commit, so history stays safe for others. Note: merging that branch again later needs the revert of the revert.

title: FileService has a constructor argument `string $storageDir`. Symfony cannot autowire a string. What is a clean fix?
options: Call new FileService() in every controller
explain: Autowiring works with classes and interfaces. For scalar values you tell Symfony the value: the #[Autowire] attribute with a parameter, or bind it in services.yaml. %kernel.project_dir% is a built-in parameter. The path then lives in one place.
